title: A wider conducting wall
hook: Change cross-sectional area and predict conducted heat rate.
misconception: conducted heat rate stays fixed when cross-sectional area doubles.
objective: Apply Q̇ = kAΔT/L to compare conducted heat rate when cross-sectional area changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With steady one-dimensional conduction with fixed thickness conductivity and temperature difference, Q̇ = kAΔT/L. When cross-sectional area doubles, conducted heat rate becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model Q̇ = kAΔT/L; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider steady one-dimensional conduction with fixed thickness conductivity and temperature difference, with a nonzero initial result. If cross-sectional area triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on conducted heat rate?
recall.why: Apply Q̇ = kAΔT/L under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
